item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded:
If I'm reading it correctly, and I could be wrong, but I think covering the statue only temporarily stops the effects. If you leave it covered, the effect will continue to grow stronger, eventually no longer needing eye contact, or even to see it at all. Though it's certainly not spelled out that way, that was the impression I got. Obviously, that might be something to add to the edit, even if it's simply an addendum about the night janitor that killed himself after they tried just covering the darn thing.

As for why it's being slated for editing, there's a major edit going on, where the senior staff is going through all the entries, and putting things up for editing that could use a bit or a lot of improvement, and outright deleting things that either aren't well done, or don't fit the site at all. I could be wrong, but it looks like yours just could use some editing to change the tone a bit, and clarify a bit.

item.title: Re:

My suggestion would be to make it a bit more succinct and less prosey.

item.title: Re:
item.content:encoded: Normally there's a timeline of how long it takes a person to be affected, and it increases over time. Originally, since it was being held along with other artwork, it had aesthetically pleasing surroundings and thus was not "angered" to use a not quite correct term. Thus the next time it was exposed to a test subject, the effects were far more intense and immediate, rather than taking over a half hour.

However, I suppose this may be a case of me 'buying into the hype', or otherwise misunderstanding some things, so I rescind my previous comment.
